correctness.rationale: The theorem is obtained from the exact simultaneous equations xv+cyu=0 and uy+cvx=0, which exhaust the zero-bracket condition. Their projective and determinant cases prove the three graph decompositions. Component clique generating functions and careful repeated-entry counting prove every tuple formula, including k=0 and k=1. The isomorphism test uses the full-rank bilinear form asymmetry operator diag(c^-1,c); reversal realizes inversion. Ten independent complete prime-field censuses verify component structures, clique coefficients and length-1,2,3 tuples; four further complete GF(9) checks verify components and two-/three-tuples, while the symbolic argument proves all odd prime powers.

value.rationale: A complete natural element-level graph and all clique/tuple enumerators refine the established 3D nilpotent Leibniz classification. For q≥7, (q-3)/2 nonisomorphic algebras have the identical generic graph, with explicit F7 witnesses c=2 and c=3. Even in the exceptional parameter pair where two-sided commuting-pair counts agree, ordered triples differ by \\(q^3(q-1)^4\\). This reveals precise information loss in graph and pair-count invariants and a structurally meaningful arity separation, not an arbitrary narrow computation.
